item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm wondering if I missed something, because this didn't really speak to me. 36 humanoid entities that negate other anomalies; is that all there is to this? The writing came off incredibly unrealistic, as in, people don't really speak like that do in these interviews. Comes off very scripted and voiceless. Again, might be missing something here, I'm a bit obtuse with figurative language.

The cross tests were honestly kind of lame and had next to no tension. The SCP-Devil-Lawyer, or at least some acquaintance thereof, using profanity all willy-nilly set an odd tone, and Cain and Able immediately being redeemed in full with no consequences left me more confused than excited. The constant talk of redemption, saving the world, the world dying, and so on, quite frankly had me rolling my eyes more than anything.

This was astoundingly well-written on a technical level, which I imagine is part of why this is upvoted as much as it is, but on a narrative level this falls flat in my opinion. I was leaning towards a downvote (as little as that matters at this point lol) but I'll just leave it alone.

item.content:encoded:
Nice work! One thing that bothered me:

SCP-001-02 - Tamil - Female - 88 - Contained - Was pregnant at time of containment. Child born without incident, currently under Foundation watch.

Was SCP-001-02 supposed to be 88 when she gave birth? Or 88 at the present?

If the former, is this acknowledged as a biological anomaly? I realize being able to give birth at 88 and holding the fate of the world in your hands don't quite have the same level of direness, but still would be something the SCP would be interested in investigating.

If the latter, is the Foundation using resources to house what would now be an adult at a max age of about 50? I would think they would either keep child contained for observation (which would be nice to have elaboration on, or its own SCP if it had anomalous properties) OR if child was normal, would be released with an amnesiac and remanded into child protective services at a young age.

Sorry if I missed an answer about this elsewhere.

Will give +1 when I know the answer :)

Right then. This is gonna get Djoricverse for a bit, so we are moving out of what is directly stated in this article and into personal myth-arcs and the like.

The world as it exists in the scipverse is essentially of two natures - how it appears to be (the normalcy the Foundation propagates), and what it actually is (the world hidden by the Flood / Masquerade).

The 36 pierce the veil around them, removing the corruptions and glitches in the universe.

Thank you.

like they'd end up wiping them out regardless of what they did

The 36 don't really wipe out anything. While the bulk of their property is negation, that's not exclusive. They don't get rid of anomalies, as much as fix them back into proper working order.

(Now this little bit is based mostly in the expanded material that came after this, and so might not entirely be reflected in this article)

The institution of the Flood after the fall of the Daevites kinda did a number on things. When you push magic out of the world, it tends to leak back in all wronglike. The 36 reorder things all proper-like, which is all part of preparing for the end of the world.

But, since the Foundation delayed them, the 36 can't get things prepared in time. The plan has gone askew.

Part of this was because the Foundation just didn't understand what was going on. Part of it was because the Foundation was so reluctant to let go of their identity and purpose. Part of it was because there are elements within the Foundation that don't want it to happen.

The King's shadow is long, his court broad, and his servants clever.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
First off, if 343 was going to be used, it would have been the version found in this tale of mine.

343 was never really on the table for addition because he's not part of the Big Picture. His mythos influence is incredibly limited; He's in the upper spectrum of human ability, but that still puts him as significantly weaker than most gods and just barely higher than most of the fair folk and local spirits (Working within the lines laid out within my body of work). A properly prepared and equipped baseline human could outwit and outmaneuver 343, and probably kill him if they set themselves to it. People have come close. In the grand scheme of things, he's a pawn with no king. Quoth Azula, "Don't flatter yourself; You were never even a player."

As for your suggestion, it's overwrought, stilted, cliche, and misses the entire point of the article. Your Thirty-Sixer there (who, might I add, is not even in Foundation custody) is pulling a bunch of holier than thou nonsense, which is the exact opposite of the entire idea of the Tzadikim Nistarim - they are the hidden holy ones. They exist in secret, even to themselves (Until this point, given the whole approaching end times and everything when some self-recognition is necessary). They're not going to go about proclaiming judgment on people, and even less likely to start executing it. Humility and mercy are kinda their thing.

A harmless old man with a silver tongue and a few cheap parlor tricks is hardly enough enough to count as…well, anything really, in a universe where you have the Scarlet King. There are actual threats to be dealt with, actual evil to deal with.

And that's why he would not be featured: it would be boring.

Essentially, you're looking for something that isn't there. The Thirty-Six are mellow

item.content:encoded:
I love this article, and I would rant about how amazing it is and why I upvoted, but that would take too long, and I just want to ask a question.
Why didn't you introduce SCP-001 to SCP-343?
In-universe, it's probably because his presence is actually beneficial to people on-site, but I'd still think the Foundation would want to neutralize his powers so they'd have one less anomaly on there hands, and hey, they neutralized 073's powers too, and he wasn't dangerous.
Out-of-universe, I don't see why not. It'd be pretty interesting.
In my headcannon, SCP-343 is just a really powerful reality bender with God complex, so it'd go like this:

<Begin Log>

[SCP-001-07 enters SCP-343's containment chamber.]
SCP-343: Good afte-… wait… are you-?
SCP-001-07: Indeed, I am.
SCP-343: No… you can't be. He doesn't exist.
SCP-001-07: Do not speak such foolish words, young one.
SCP-343: He doesn't fucking exist!
SCP-001-07: [chuckles] It is amusing to hear you say that; a heretic that does not believe in the one that he is masquerading as.
SCP-343: He doesn't exist. Your God doesn't exist because I am God!
SCP-001-07: No, you are not God. You are imperfect, just like everyone else. You are nothing more than a man with abnormal power, and every breath you take blasphemies him. Pray that He is merciful towards you, for I will not be.
SCP-343: [Incoherent screaming]

[At this point, SCP-343 attempted to terminate SCP-001-07, but was unable to succeed, due to its lack of anomalous powers. SCP-343 subsequently assaulted SCP-001-07 with its bare hands, but was incapacitated by guards before any critical damage could be dealt to SCP-001-07. SCP-343 has been reclassified as SCP-343-N.]
<End Log>

Closing Statement: SCP-343-N is currently being held in the ██████ Asylum due to its God complex and overall mental instability.
